summary: An I2C monitor that measures the voltage across a shunt resistor and the bus voltage. After you program a calibration value it also reports current and power directly.

cite.q: 01 Shunt voltage Shunt voltage measurement data.
02 Bus voltage Bus voltage measurement data.

facts.text: The shunt voltage register counts in 10 microvolt steps.
The bus voltage register counts in 4 mV steps, after shifting right by three bits.
The bus voltage value sits in bits 15 to 3; shift right by three before applying the 4 mV step.

cite.q: must be shifted right by three bits

facts.text: The power register's step is fixed at 20 times Current_LSB.
Current register = shunt register x calibration / 4096.
Power register = current register x bus register / 5000.
The datasheet's worked example (20 mV across 2 mOhm, 12 V bus, 1 mA/bit) gives calibration 20480, shifted bus value 2995, current 10000 and power 5990. The simulator reproduces all four.

all: results in a calibration value of 20480 (5000h)
equal to BB3h, the decimal equivalent of 2995
the result of 10000 (2710h) is automatically loaded
the result of 5990 (1766h) is automatically loaded

facts.text: Bit 0 of the Calibration register is not used in the calculation.

cite.q: bit FS0 is not used in the calculation

facts.text: Writing 1 to Configuration bit 15 resets every register to its default; the bit clears itself.

cite.q: Resets all registers to default values; this bit self-clears.

facts.text: Configuration bit 13 picks the bus range: 0 is 16 V, 1 is 32 V (default).
Configuration bits 12:11 set the shunt PGA: /1 is +-40 mV, /2 +-80 mV, /4 +-160 mV, /8 +-320 mV (default).

notModeled: ADC resolution, averaging and conversion time: registers follow the inputs immediately
Operating modes (power-down, triggered): the MODE bits are stored but ignored
The CNVR and OVF flags in the bus voltage register (always read as 0 here)
